SEC11A-02.note: Long subject with nonrestrictive 'which...and which...' clause opened by a comma; closing comma before main verb 'shows'. A folds 'shows' into the relative clause leaving no main verb (tempting); D dash mismatches the opening comma; C leaves a fragment. PHASE 2: key and explanation agree with my cold solve; path coherent.

SEC11A-03.note: Second sentence has a noun-clause subject ('That the two...descend...was not demonstrated'), so a full boundary is required. A misreads as relative clause, B splice, D 'so that' subordinates and strands 'was'. Resolving verb 'was' is far beyond four words, which is what makes it hard. PHASE 2: key and explanation agree with my cold solve; path coherent.

SEC11A-04.note: 'Its oak hull...had begun' is an independent clause; A splice (looks like an absolute but has a finite verb), B run-on, C 'with' strands 'had begun' without a subject. PHASE 2: key and path correct. Same splice/run-on/comma+preposition/boundary template as A-06 and close to B-05; fine alone, but three near-clones in 12 items lets a student solve by template.

SEC11A-06.note: Same template as A-04: splice / run-on / comma+preposition / correct boundary. C 'alongside' strands 'now suggest' without a subject. PHASE 2: key and path correct. Template clone of A-04 (', the' / no mark / ', alongside the' / '; the').
